answer: Each identity anchors to one registered offshore mooring anchor with a GPS buoy. Every epoch the buoy signs a reading: sun zenith angle, wave height, and its wander track inside the anchor's watch circle, bound to the epoch nonce and checked against tide tables. Two identities sharing one anchor report the same track, collapse to one vote, and burn a $60 stake. A farm wanting 100 votes must buy, deploy, and service 100 real anchors at $3,000 each plus $200 yearly upkeep, with a boat visit per buoy; an honest sailor anchors once and certifies one buoy per epoch, so cost grows linearly with n.
